does: Cuts food so fine that it melts into a dish and leaves no piece to bite on.

intro.what: Mincing cuts food very finely so distinct pieces do not stand out in the dish.
intro.why: It teaches you to recognise an even fine cut and prepare strong aromatics close to when they are needed.

how: Slice the food thinly, then cut across the slices.
Rock the knife over the pile, scraping it together now and then, until no piece stands out.
For garlic, crush the clove under the flat of the blade first, so that the skin slips off and the flesh breaks open.

cues.text: A fine, moist pile with no piece larger than a grain.
Garlic smells sharp and strong the moment it is cut this fine.

mistakes.mistake: Mincing garlic long before it is needed, so that it turns harsh.
mistakes.fix: Mince it last, just before it goes into the pan.

quiz.question: Why mince an aromatic rather than leave large pieces?
choices: So it blends into the dish without large pieces to bite on.
So a few bites contain most of the aromatic.
So every piece stays large and distinct.
quiz.because: Very fine cutting lets the food blend in rather than remain as noticeable chunks.

quiz.question: How do you keep the pile together as you mince?
choices: Spread the pieces widely and stop gathering them.
Rock the knife and scrape the pile together as needed.
Press once with the blade and leave the pieces coarse.
quiz.because: Gathering the pile lets repeated rocking cuts reach the remaining larger pieces.

quiz.question: What should the finished pile look like?
choices: Long strips mixed with large chunks.
A few whole cloves beside finely cut pieces.
Fine and even with no piece standing out.
quiz.because: An even fine pile shows the larger pieces have been cut down consistently.

quiz.question: Garlic tastes harsh after being minced long ahead. What would you change next time?
choices: Mince it just before it goes into the pan.
Mince it earlier and leave it exposed longer.
Crush it into finer pieces far in advance.
quiz.because: Preparing minced garlic close to use avoids the harshness described after a long wait.

variant_of.differs: It goes on much longer, until the pieces are almost a paste and vanish into the dish.
